determinism.note: All optimizers use fixed iteration/expansion/population counts and a seeded RNG; no wall-clock cutoff is used anywhere in the planner (spec 13).

L1.definition: known parameters, ideal continuous three-axis body torque saturated at 5.8 N*m per axis, no fault, no slosh, no sensor noise, no command delay, no minimum pulse width
L1.harness: src/sim/challenge-v3/levels.ts runLevel1 - integrates the audited integrateWithCollision with the torque injected through u.tauThrO; the audited physics files are untouched
L1.verdict: PASS - the basic pointing problem is solved in this inertia and torque envelope, so a stage-1 failure cannot be attributed to basic control

L2.definition: known parameters, real 40 ms pulse quantisation, 120 ms command delay, two-thruster concurrency, single thruster failure, fuel constraint, truth state readable
L2.note: The measured stage-1 run is L2 with the slosh and slider subsystems left active, i.e. strictly harder than the minimal L2 definition; it is the same run reported in truth-optimizer-train10.json.
L2.verdict: FAIL - the level that fails is the discrete-actuation level, with L1 passing at 100%. Per specification section 5 this failure MUST NOT be attributed to the estimator.

L3.reason: Specification section 7 requires that observation-only development stop when the truth-state Train-10 gate fails. The gate failed (attitude 70% against a 90% requirement), so estimation, active identification, belief-rollout calibration and observation-only planning were not attempted and no numbers are reported for them. This is a halt mandated by the specification, not a claim that these stages are infeasible.
L3.definition: real thrusters, single fault, observation-only, eta_T unknown, slosh off or known

L4.reason: Specification section 7 requires that observation-only development stop when the truth-state Train-10 gate fails. The gate failed (attitude 70% against a 90% requirement), so estimation, active identification, belief-rollout calibration and observation-only planning were not attempted and no numbers are reported for them. This is a halt mandated by the specification, not a claim that these stages are infeasible.

localisation: L1 passes 10/10 with terminal attitude 0.004-0.010 deg and terminal rate below 2e-4 rad/s. The same scenarios fail at L2. The loss is therefore created entirely by the discrete action space (40 ms quantum, two-thruster concurrency, 120 ms delay) and by the finite search over action sequences, not by control-theoretic authority, not by the estimator, and not by fuel.
